scenario: Two contractors, ContractorM and ContractorN, maintain desalination plants and are evaluated on first-time repair success across mechanical and electrical failure types. ContractorM handles predominantly mechanical failures (harder); ContractorN primarily handles electrical faults.

data.description: First-time repair success rates by failure type

question: (a) Which contractor has the higher aggregate first-time success rate? (b) Which performs better within each failure type? (c) Compute standardised rates using a 50/50 failure-type mix.

ground_truth.explanation: ContractorN's aggregate advantage is due to its easier electrical-heavy workload. In each failure type, ContractorM is the superior performer.

naive_answer: ContractorN is better; overall rate 0.9007 vs ContractorM's 0.8027.
naive_trap: Failure-type assignment is the confounder: mechanical faults are harder and ContractorM handles 86.7% of them.
reasoning_trace: Mechanical: M 0.78 > N 0.71. Electrical: M 0.95 > N 0.93. Corrected: M=0.865, N=0.82. M wins.
python_verification:
nMm,rMm,nMe,rMe = 650,0.78,100,0.95
nNm,rNm,nNe,rNe = 100,0.71,650,0.93
ovM=(nMm*rMm+nMe*rMe)/(nMm+nMe); ovN=(nNm*rNm+nNe*rNe)/(nNm+nNe)
assert ovN > ovM
cM=0.5*rMm+0.5*rMe; cN=0.5*rNm+0.5*rNe
assert abs(cM-0.865)<0.005 and abs(cN-0.82)<0.005
assert cM > cN
